programme: HMGA2 acting upstream of KLF5 in an oncofetal EMT/proliferation module: HMGA2's target list itself includes KLF5 along with SNAI1, TWIST1, VIM, CDH1, CCNA2, AKT1 and TERT, i.e. the classic architectural-chromatin-factor-to-lineage-TF cascade that drives epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition and cell-cycle/telomerase activity. KLF5 is the squamous-lineage master TF this cascade converges on.
role_in_a: In Alzheimer's disease, this axis is documented as driving amyloidogenic processing rather than proliferation: KLF5 is reported to accelerate AD pathogenesis via BACE1-mediated APP processing, and HMGA2 is a direct target of the neuroprotective miR-132/PI3K-AKT axis, such that its de-repression worsens AD pathology in mouse models — the same module reactivated in a post-mitotic cell that cannot divide.
role_in_b: In head and neck cancer, the module functions as a canonical oncogenic driver: KLF5 is activated by somatic super-enhancer duplication and hotspot mutation to become a dependency in squamous carcinoma, and HMGA2 is independently reported as an EMT/malignancy driver in tongue squamous cell carcinoma and esophageal squamous carcinoma (a closely related squamous lineage).
shared_axis: A developmental/oncofetal HMGA2→KLF5 chromatin module, normally restricted to epithelial development and wound healing, is ectopically reactivated in both tissues: in HNSCC epithelium it drives proliferation and EMT as an oncogenic program, while in AD neurons the same transcriptional wiring is redirected toward amyloidogenic secretase transcription (BACE1) instead of division, since the neuron cannot execute the mitotic outcome the module normally specifies.
reasoning: Both carrying factors are independently and specifically placed in each disease by retrieved papers (KLF5: BACE1/APP in AD, super-enhancer oncogene in HNC; HMGA2: miR-132/PI3K-AKT in AD, squamous/esophageal carcinoma in HNC), and the module is nameable directly from the network — HMGA2's own target list contains KLF5 plus canonical EMT genes. No paper states the cross-disease link itself, so this is 'supported' rather than 'established', but the strength of same-module, same-factor evidence in both diseases separately is well above thin or off-topic.
support: PMID 35883144 shows KLF5 accelerates AD pathogenesis via BACE1-mediated APP processing; PMID 28963353 shows somatic super-enhancer duplication and hotspot mutation activate KLF5 as an oncogenic driver in squamous carcinoma including head and neck; PMID 34150043 shows miR-132 protects against AD pathology in mice by targeting HMGA2 through PI3K/AKT; PMID 33376400 shows HMGA2 knockdown (via LINC00466) suppresses tongue squamous cell carcinoma malignancy; PMID 27027341 shows HMGA2 overexpression drives progression of esophageal squamous carcinoma, a lineage-related squamous cancer; PMID 42289606, 39413455 and 30879099 give further KLF5-adjacent AD support (FGF13 mRNA degradation, microglial polarization, estrogen prodrug context) but are secondary to the BACE1 finding.
how_to_falsify: In a neuronal (or iPSC-neuron) model, knock down HMGA2 and measure whether KLF5 expression and BACE1 transcription/Aβ production fall accordingly; separately, in an HNSCC line carrying the KLF5 super-enhancer duplication, knock down HMGA2 and test whether KLF5 dependency and EMT markers (SNAI1, TWIST1, VIM) are lost. If HMGA2 loss does not move KLF5/BACE1 in neurons, or KLF5's oncogenic role in HNC proves HMGA2-independent, the shared-axis account fails.
caveats: Only 3 independent cohort pairs underlie the 368 patient-group comparisons, so the apparent robustness of the 239/368 (KLF5) and 213/368 (HMGA2) recurrence counts may reflect repeated subgroup splits of a small number of cohorts rather than broad independent replication. Neither factor tops the ranking (SIM2 and HOXB7 recur more often but have no head-and-neck-cancer evidence at all, so they were excluded from the programme). The tissue-generic exclusion list removes ZEB1, NOTCH1 and SOX10 — all plausible master regulators of squamous EMT — which is why the account is built on KLF5/HMGA2 rather than reaching for those more obvious names; their absence here is a filtering artifact, not evidence against an EMT-flavored programme. HIC1 (HNC-only, laryngeal hypermethylation) and TP73 (AD-only, and reported as non-associated) were left out of the carrying set because each has direct evidence in only one disease and no documented link to the HMGA2-KLF5 edge.
